n: The book closes by noting the king’s power: he imposed taxes across his empire, even on distant coastlands. Life in the empire went on — but now with a faithful Jew at the king’s side.

f.g: Coastlands and islands, such as those in the Mediterranean.

n: The king’s deeds and Mordecai’s greatness were recorded in the official chronicles of Persia — a formula like those used for Israel’s kings, inviting readers to see this as real history.

f.w: are they not written in the book of the chronicles

n: Mordecai becomes second only to the king and is loved by his people. He used his power to seek their good and speak peace for their future — a model of righteous leadership.

f.w: seeking the wealth of his people
